reviewBoundary: Eight explicitly authored original complete paired-reading practices. Each group has two full passages with five four-option questions each; frozen originals provide level and task structure only. Same-author entailment, unique-key and all-distractor audit, not independent teacher/learner calibration, official CET provenance, publication or production approval.

units.title: 四级阅读：幼苗弯曲的方向与旧书重新装订的痕迹

materials.title: The Seedling That Turned towards the Window
materials.text:
A classroom placed young seedlings beside a window. After several days, some stems curved towards the light. A student described the plants as walking across their pots to reach a brighter place. The teacher used the description to ask which part had changed and how the change had happened.

The roots and the pot had not crossed the table. The observation concerned a change in the growing stem’s form. Under the conditions discussed, unequal growth on different sides could bend the stem. The curve was therefore not evidence that the entire plant had travelled like an animal. The teacher separated movement produced through growth from a change in the location of the whole organism.

The class compared the direction of illumination with the stem’s position over time. A still picture of a curved plant could show its present shape, but would not by itself establish the sequence that produced it. Keeping the earlier views made the change examinable. The students also recorded how the pots had been placed so a later rotation would not be mistaken for an unexplained reversal of the response.

The teacher did not conclude that light was the only influence on plant form. The particular comparison supported a question about the direction of light under stated conditions. A different question could require further comparisons, including attention to the plant’s growth stage and other relevant conditions. The class retained that distinction rather than turning one familiar example into a rule about every bend in every plant.

The final display showed a dated sequence and a description of the part observed. It replaced the charming but misleading image of a walking plant with something more interesting: an organism could change its form in relation to its surroundings while remaining rooted in place. The explanation depended on following the change, not merely giving the final shape an appealing story.

questions.prompt: Why was walking a misleading description?
options: The pots had crossed the table by themselves.
The observed change was stem curvature through growth rather than travel of the entire plant.
The seedlings could not grow at all.
The teacher said no part of a plant could ever change position.
questions.explanation: B正确：根盆没整体迁移，茎差生长弯曲非动物步行。A反事实；C有长；D非否局部变化。

questions.prompt: What did the dated views add beyond one still picture?
options: They guaranteed light was the only possible influence.
They proved every species responded identically.
They removed the need to note pot placement.
They helped establish the sequence of shape change.
questions.explanation: D正确：时序可核形如何变，单照只现态。A不排他因；C须记放盆；B未普种。

questions.prompt: Why record whether a pot was rotated?
options: A changed placement could affect how later stem direction was interpreted.
The class wanted to hide interventions.
Rotation could never change any reference direction.
A rotation proved the whole plant walked.
questions.explanation: A正确：后转盆需史免误解响应逆转，与照光参照相关。C错；B要明；D非走。

questions.prompt: How broad was the supported conclusion?
options: It explained every curved plant under all conditions.
It proved growth stage never mattered.
It concerned directional light and stem change in the stated comparison.
It made all further comparisons unnecessary.
questions.explanation: C正确：限定此比较光向与茎变，别问还需控制与阶段。A、B、D均过推。

questions.prompt: What makes the final explanation informative?
options: It follows the observed part and its change over time rather than relying only on an attractive story.
It describes every bend as deliberate walking.
It ignores the earlier positions.
It replaces observations with a claim about all plants.
questions.explanation: A正确：末段定部位时序供生长解释，不拟人编终形故事。B错误；C保旧视；D拒泛化。

materials.title: The Notes inside the Binding
materials.text:
A college library received an old textbook with a loose cover. Its pages contained handwritten notes by several readers. A student offered to make it look new by replacing the cover, trimming the edges and removing the marked blank pages. The librarian first asked what the library wanted to preserve.

The book was not kept only for the printed lesson. Its use history was part of the collection’s interest. A reader’s note could refer to a particular printed paragraph, and a small mark at an edge might connect with another sign elsewhere. Cutting or discarding material could remove evidence even if every printed sentence remained legible.

The librarian distinguished repair for use from an attempt to recreate an imagined new condition. A stronger binding could help people handle the book, but a visually neat result was not the only criterion. The team documented the existing order and marks before deciding on treatment. It did not assume that every stain was valuable or that no alteration was ever possible. The decision depended on the object’s role and the information at risk.

A replacement cover was identified as new. The record did not make it appear that the book had always had that cover. Where an original part was retained separately, its relationship with the volume remained clear. A future reader could then distinguish the historical object from the library’s later work on it.

The final treatment improved handling while preserving the relevant marked material. The book still looked used. That appearance did not mean the repair had failed. It reflected a decision about what made this particular copy worth keeping. The student learned that restoring access to an object and restoring a supposedly perfect appearance were different tasks. Good repair began with knowing which task mattered and how a proposed change would affect the evidence the object carried.

questions.prompt: Why could trimming remove evidence despite preserving printed sentences?
options: Printed text was the only information the library valued.
Every mark was made by the same reader.
Annotations and edge marks could record relationships and use history.
The pages had no handwriting.
questions.explanation: C正确：手注边标可能互连印段及使用史，印文不等全信息。A反；B多读者；D明有。

questions.prompt: What guided the repair decision?
options: The copy’s collection role and the information a treatment might affect.
Refusing every possible alteration.
Making the copy look completely unused at any cost.
Removing all nonprinted material automatically.
questions.explanation: A正确：先定本物角色证据风险，非全污珍贵亦非全不改。C、B两极；D手注需保。

questions.prompt: Why identify a replacement cover as new?
options: To claim it had always been attached.
To erase the original book’s history.
To make future checking impossible.
To distinguish later repair from the object’s earlier state.
questions.explanation: D正确：新封要标和工作留史，不能假从来如此。A反；B保史；C供未来分辨。

questions.prompt: Why was a used appearance compatible with success?
options: The binding had been left loose by definition.
The treatment aimed at handling and relevant evidence rather than a universal appearance of newness.
Every stain was proved historically important.
The librarian required all printed text to disappear.
questions.explanation: B正确：成功按易用与保重要标记，旧观可为目的结果。A改善拿用；C非每污宝；D保文。

questions.prompt: Which distinction did the student learn?
options: Access and appearance must always be identical goals.
A new cover automatically becomes historical evidence of original manufacture.
Improving access to a copy can differ from making it appear perfectly new.
Repair should begin before knowing the object’s purpose.
questions.explanation: C正确：末段修访问与仿完美新貌异，要先任务及证据影响。A混同；B新旧须分；D先定目的。

units.title: 四级阅读：预点单的等待时间与果实采后成熟

materials.title: The Queue Had Moved to the Kitchen
materials.text:
A fictional campus café introduced advance ordering. Customers could choose and pay before arriving, then collect at a separate counter. The visible line at the payment desk became shorter. A publicity draft claimed that the café had eliminated waiting from the entire service.

The supervisor examined the complete route of an order. Choosing, payment, preparation and collection were different stages. Moving one stage to a phone could reduce the time spent at the payment desk while leaving preparation delays elsewhere. Some customers waited after arrival; others waited away from the café while their food was being made. The absence of a long physical line did not show that every order was completed immediately.

The team measured time from stated starting and ending events. A customer’s arrival-to-collection interval answered a different question from order-submission-to-collection time. Both could be useful, but a change in one did not automatically imply the same change in the other. The report named the interval instead of placing an unexplained number beside the word faster.

Advance orders also changed the kitchen’s information. Staff could see some demand earlier and organise preparation accordingly. That could improve the process under the café’s conditions, but it did not create unlimited capacity. A large group ordering for the same moment could still produce a difficult peak. The team retained that variation in its observations rather than reporting only a quiet hour.

The revised announcement said what had improved and which waiting measure had been used. It did not dismiss the new system because waiting remained. Nor did it confuse a shorter visible queue with the disappearance of all delay. The café’s lesson was to follow the service across stages. A good interface could change where and how people waited, while the complete experience still depended on preparation, timing and the demand placed on the system.

questions.prompt: Why did a shorter payment line not prove waiting had disappeared?
options: Every customer spent identical time at every stage.
All orders were physically completed before submission.
The kitchen had no role in the service.
Preparation and collection could still involve delays elsewhere in the order’s route.
questions.explanation: D正确：手机移选付阶段不消制作领取等延迟，可能场外等。B倒序；C厨房重要；A时间异。

questions.prompt: Why name the start and end of a waiting measure?
options: To guarantee all intervals changed identically.
Different endpoints answer different questions about the service.
To make timing impossible.
Because collection was never observed.
questions.explanation: B正确：到店取餐与提交取餐问不同，须明端点，非都faster。A不保同；C便量；D有取。

questions.prompt: What potential benefit came from earlier demand information?
options: It made preparation capacity infinite.
It prevented all peaks.
It could help staff organise preparation before arrival.
It proved every quiet-hour result applied to a busy group.
questions.explanation: C正确：预知部分需求可安排，但同期群单仍峰。A无限错；B不防全；D样时不能通化。

questions.prompt: How did the revised report treat remaining waiting?
options: As compatible with a specified improvement in part of the service.
As something to hide by reporting only quiet periods.
As equivalent to failure of every advance order.
As proof no aspect had improved.
questions.explanation: A正确：可改部分同时仍等，须具体指标，不全否新系统。D、C极端；B保variation。

questions.prompt: What approach does the passage recommend?
options: Judge the kitchen only by payment-screen colour.
Follow the order across stages rather than infer the whole experience from one visible line.
Treat every phone order as instantly finished.
Remove the definitions of timing measures.
questions.explanation: B正确：完整服务路径和需求时序共同，短线非全体验。A无关；C错；D要定义。

materials.title: The Fruit Continued to Change
materials.text:
A produce class compared harvested fruits stored under stated conditions. One variety continued to develop a softer texture and a different aroma after picking. Another did not develop the desired qualities in the same way. A student concluded that taking fruit off the plant either stopped all biology or improved every fruit automatically, and asked which rule was correct.

The tutor rejected the choice between those two universal statements. A harvested fruit could remain biologically active. Its changes depended on the kind of fruit, its stage at harvest and the conditions afterwards. The ability of one variety to continue ripening did not show that every unripe fruit could be picked at any stage and later become equally good.

The class distinguished ripening from deterioration. Changes associated with desirable eating qualities were not identical to every process that eventually made produce unusable. A softer fruit might be ready for one purpose or damaged for another. The record therefore described what had changed and how the intended use was judged, rather than giving all softness one fixed meaning.

The samples were observed over time. A photograph of an attractive surface did not directly measure internal texture or aroma. The group combined its stated observations instead of assuming a single colour supplied a complete maturity test for every variety. It also kept the harvest stage with the storage history so differences were not attributed to one factor whose conditions had actually changed alongside others.

The final display showed why a living product could change after separation from the plant without following one universal timetable. It offered no instruction for storing an unknown crop. Its conclusion concerned the described comparison: the meaning of a later change depended on the fruit, its earlier state, the environment and the quality being considered. Asking those questions was more useful than assuming either that nothing happened after picking or that every later change was an improvement.

questions.prompt: Why were both proposed universal rules rejected?
options: Post-harvest activity and its useful effects varied with fruit, stage and conditions.
Every harvested fruit was already dead.
Every fruit necessarily improved at the same rate.
Harvest stage could never affect the result.
questions.explanation: A正确：可仍活跃但依类阶段后境，不是全停或自动全好。B、C极端错；D阶段重要。

questions.prompt: What distinction does the tutor make about softness?
options: Softness always means ideal eating quality.
Softness has no observable meaning.
Softness proves every fruit was picked at the same stage.
Its interpretation can depend on process and intended use rather than a universal good-or-bad label.
questions.explanation: D正确：成熟品质与败坏不同，同软依用途可合或损，需记变化。A一律好错；B可观；C不证同摘时。

questions.prompt: Why was an attractive surface photograph insufficient?
options: It measured every aroma directly.
It did not directly establish all internal texture and aroma qualities.
The class had no other observations.
It guaranteed identical internal states.
questions.explanation: B正确：表照不直接量内质香，需合观察而非万能色标。A、D错误；C有多观察。

questions.prompt: Why retain harvest stage with storage history?
options: To remove information about earlier states.
To prove storage never mattered.
To avoid attributing differences to one factor when relevant conditions differed together.
To make every variety identical.
questions.explanation: C正确：阶段及存史保才能审共变，不能单归未隔离因素。B存境重要；A保早态；D不变物种。

questions.prompt: Which conclusion fits the passage?
options: A later change must be interpreted through fruit type, prior state, conditions and the quality of interest.
Every post-harvest change is deterioration.
No biological process can continue after picking.
One variety establishes a universal storage timetable.
questions.explanation: A正确：末段四者定后变含义，非两极或普时表。B成熟不全坏；C可活；D不通化。

units.title: 四级阅读：同音词的语境与共享工作室的预订状态

materials.title: A Word the Ear Could Not Choose Alone
materials.text:
A language club listened to a short invented sentence containing two words that sounded alike in the accent used. On a worksheet, the choices had different spellings and meanings. One learner argued that anyone who could hear clearly must be able to identify the intended spelling from the sound alone.

The tutor explained that the ambiguity was genuine under the stated pronunciation. Better hearing would not necessarily supply a distinction that the speaker had not produced. The surrounding sentence and situation could help select a meaning. This was a matter of using language in context, not automatically a failure of the listener’s ears.

The club compared the isolated sound with the complete sentence. In one context, the topic made one interpretation plausible. In another, both remained possible until a later phrase or a question clarified the intention. The tutor did not force a final choice when the evidence supported more than one reading. A useful answer could state what remained ambiguous and ask for the needed information.

Writing provided a different set of clues. The two spellings could separate the words visibly, but the written form was not a second sound secretly present in the recording. The lesson kept spoken evidence and written evidence distinct. It also named the accent used, because words that sound identical in one pronunciation need not do so in every other.

For practice, learners wrote brief contexts rather than repeating the same isolated sound more loudly. They learned to explain which part of the context supported a choice. The activity did not claim that sound was irrelevant to understanding. It showed how sound, grammar, meaning and situation could contribute different information. Good listening sometimes involved recognising the limit of the signal and finding another route to the speaker’s intended message, rather than insisting that every uncertainty could be solved by listening harder to exactly the same sound.

questions.prompt: Why might clearer hearing fail to select the spelling?
options: Every accent necessarily pronounced the words identically.
The learner was forbidden to use context.
The stated pronunciation contained no distinguishing sound between the two words.
Writing and speech were the same evidence by definition.
questions.explanation: C正确：该口音同音本无区别，不是听清就能得未发音差。B可用境；A非全口音；D分证据。

questions.prompt: What did the full sentence add?
options: Context that could support an interpretation, though some cases remained uncertain.
A guarantee that ambiguity always disappeared.
A hidden written letter inside the sound.
Proof that sound never matters.
questions.explanation: A正确：全句主题可约义，有些仍需后词澄清，非总解。B绝对；C无暗字；D声亦贡献。

questions.prompt: What response was appropriate when both meanings remained possible?
options: Pretend the preferred answer was certain.
Repeat the sound as proof one spelling was wrong.
Declare every listener unable to hear.
State the ambiguity and seek relevant clarification.
questions.explanation: D正确：不强定，明未决求需要信息。A假确定；B同音反复不补区别；C非聋。

questions.prompt: Why name the accent?
options: To prove all other pronunciations were incorrect.
Because the sound relationship could differ under another pronunciation.
To show spelling was audible in every recording.
To make context unnecessary.
questions.explanation: B正确：同音依所用发音，其他口音可能有区别。A未评别错；D还境；C书写非音内。

questions.prompt: Why write brief contexts for practice?
options: To prove louder repetition creates a missing distinction.
To replace all listening with spelling tests.
To show how additional linguistic and situational information supports interpretation.
To ensure no word ever remains ambiguous.
questions.explanation: C正确：练写境并指哪线索支持，联合声语法义境。B未废听；A不靠响；D可仍歧。

materials.title: An Empty Studio That Was Still Booked
materials.text:
A college shared an art studio through a booking system. A visitor arrived early and saw the room empty. She began setting up a large project, assuming the absence of a person meant the absence of any reservation. A booked group arrived shortly afterwards with equipment that needed the whole room.

The coordinator explained that physical occupation and booking status were different records. A reservation concerned a defined interval and the arrangements attached to it. Someone could be travelling to the studio during the first part of an authorised setup period. An empty room at one instant did not establish that anyone could claim it for an unlimited activity.

The system displayed both the activity time and any included preparation or clearing period. Those intervals were not automatically spare gaps. The coordinator asked users to check the current entry rather than infer availability from the most visible start time on a poster. A booking’s purpose could require work before the public activity began.

Requests also had a status. Submitting a form did not immediately guarantee acceptance, and an old message about a possible time was not the same as a confirmed entry. The coordinator made confirmation explicit so users did not each arrive with a different private understanding of the same room.

The college added a short availability display outside the studio and a contact route for questions. It kept unnecessary personal details out of that public view. Users needed to know the relevant status and time, not the private information of every participant. The change helped connect the physical room with its current arrangement.

The visitor moved her project under the coordinator’s direction and later booked an appropriate period. The event was used to explain a practical distinction: seeing no one establishes a local observation, while deciding whether a resource is available requires the rule and record governing its use. A room can be momentarily empty and still belong to a scheduled activity.

questions.prompt: What assumption caused the conflict?
options: All studio bookings were cancelled.
A momentarily empty room was treated as unreserved and freely available.
The arriving group had no confirmed arrangement.
Preparation time was always excluded from bookings.
questions.explanation: B正确：物理无人不等没预订无限占，后到组有含setup安排。A、C无据；D可含准备。

questions.prompt: Why display preparation and clearing intervals?
options: They were always spare time for any visitor.
They proved the activity required no equipment.
They could be part of the authorised use even outside the public activity time.
They replaced every need for confirmation.
questions.explanation: C正确：预订可包布撤，海报明时非全使用域，不能当空隙。A反；B有设备；D请求还需确认。

questions.prompt: What is the difference between submitting and confirming a request?
options: A request could exist without the accepted arrangement recorded in the system.
Every old possibility was a current booking.
A form’s existence guaranteed acceptance.
They were identical events.
questions.explanation: A正确：提交不自动批准，旧可能消息非当前确认。D混同；B过时；C未必收。

questions.prompt: Why limit the public display’s personal details?
options: Only personal details could establish time intervals.
Users needed every participant’s address to interpret a booking.
Privacy required hiding whether the room was booked at all.
Availability decisions needed relevant status and time rather than every participant’s private information.
questions.explanation: D正确：公示所需状态时间够，不必私信息，仍助对齐房与安排。B、A无据；C可公开必要状态。

questions.prompt: Which principle does the event illustrate?
options: Any empty resource is permanently available.
A physical observation of emptiness must be connected with the rules and records governing access.
Confirmed reservations disappear whenever users travel.
An early arrival always overrides a booking.
questions.explanation: B正确：末段无人只现场观察，availability按规则记录。A、C、D错误扩大。

units.title: 四级阅读：雨量深度与陶釉试片的适用范围

materials.title: The Rain Was Deep without a Deep Puddle
materials.text:
A school weather report said that a storm produced a particular depth of rainfall. A student looked at a sloping path, found no puddle of that depth and declared the report impossible. The weather-club tutor asked what the reported depth represented and what had happened to water on the path.

Rainfall depth described the amount spread over a horizontal area under the measurement convention. Water landing on the path could run away, enter the ground or collect elsewhere. The current depth of a puddle therefore depended on local movement and storage as well as incoming rain. It was not automatically a direct copy of the storm’s rainfall total.

The club distinguished depth from volume. The same depth over a larger area represented a larger volume of water. A small gauge could support a depth measurement through its known collection geometry, but the number of litres in that container was not the volume falling on every surrounding field. The reference area had to remain part of the interpretation.

Time mattered too. The same total over a brief interval and over a long interval represented different average intensities. A daily total alone did not reveal the exact pattern of every short burst. The club retained the recording period and avoided treating one convenient total as a complete account of the storm’s timing.

The gauge also represented a location. Rain could vary across the area, so one measurement did not automatically establish identical conditions at every nearby site. The tutor used the report as evidence within its stated place and period, rather than rejecting measurement because water had moved away from a path.

The student’s observation remained useful: it described the path after the storm. The error was to make it answer a different question without accounting for runoff, area and time. Once those quantities were distinguished, the report and the dry-looking slope no longer needed to contradict each other.

questions.prompt: Why could a path lack a puddle matching rainfall depth?
options: Water could run off, enter the ground or collect elsewhere after falling.
Rainfall could never be measured.
Every path was a sealed level container.
The report necessarily described the current puddle.
questions.explanation: A正确：降水后流渗存异，当前积水非雨深直接复制。B可量；C斜坡非容器；D测雨非现水坑。

questions.prompt: What does equal depth over a larger area imply?
options: An identical total volume regardless of area.
No water fell on the larger area.
A larger volume under the stated spread-over-area meaning.
A deeper local puddle at every point by definition.
questions.explanation: C正确：深×面积体积，等深大面积大体积。A错；B非零；D非局部滞水。

questions.prompt: Why retain the measurement period?
options: It proves every minute had the daily average.
Equal totals over different durations can imply different average intensities.
Area becomes irrelevant whenever time is known.
A daily total directly shows every short burst.
questions.explanation: B正确：同总不同历时平均强度异，日量不揭精细序。A、D误；C面积仍需。

questions.prompt: What limit applies to one gauge?
options: It directly measures every nearby location identically.
Its container volume is the entire region’s rain volume.
It needs no place information.
It represents a location and does not automatically establish uniform rain across the region.
questions.explanation: D正确：雨有空间异，一点限其位，不自动全域同。A、B放大；C需地点。

questions.prompt: How is the student’s path observation treated?
options: As useful local evidence that should not be confused with the rainfall quantity.
As proof all measurements are false.
As a direct measurement of every storm’s intensity.
As evidence that runoff never happens.
questions.explanation: A正确：后雨坡况仍有用但问异，需流面积时间连结。B极端；C不量全时；D流可有。

materials.title: The Glaze Tile That Came Out Blue
materials.text:
A pottery class tested a glaze on a small tile. The fired sample appeared blue and glossy. A student expected that putting the same named glaze on any vessel would guarantee the exact same surface. The tutor placed the tile beside notes about its material and firing history.

The sample recorded a particular combination. The clay body, the glaze layer and the firing conditions could all affect the appearance. A thick application and a thin one were not necessarily equivalent. Nor was a sample placed in one part of a kiln guaranteed the same history as every other object. The glaze’s name identified a material within an arrangement; it did not erase the arrangement.

The tutor also distinguished a flat tile from a curved vessel. A surface on a cup could receive or hold material differently from a small level test piece. An attractive tile was useful for exploring possibilities, but it did not settle every practical issue for a different shape or use.

The class recorded the sample’s clay, application and stated firing conditions. It kept the physical tile with those notes so later users could inspect the result actually obtained. A photograph helped document colour but depended on lighting and display, so it was not treated as an exact replacement for the object in every visual comparison.

The student prepared a more relevant trial under the tutor’s supervised process before making the exhibition vessel. The first tile was not discarded as a failure. It remained evidence about its own conditions and a starting point for the next question.

The lesson did not provide a firing recipe or declare a real object suitable for every purpose. It showed how a sample could be informative without becoming a universal guarantee. A better prediction connected the desired result with material, form, application and process, then checked the aspects that changed rather than assuming one appealing surface had answered everything.

questions.prompt: Why did the glaze name not guarantee an identical result?
options: Names always described no real material.
Every kiln position necessarily had an identical history.
The tutor said samples could never be informative.
Clay, layer and firing conditions also contributed to the appearance.
questions.explanation: D正确：同釉名不消坯层烧成组合，厚薄位置史可异。A有标材作用；C样有用；B不保同。

questions.prompt: Why could a flat tile be insufficient for a curved vessel?
options: The tile had no observable surface.
Form could change how material was applied or held.
Every shape held glaze identically.
The vessel’s intended use was irrelevant by definition.
questions.explanation: B正确：曲器形与平片施附不同，仍有实际用途问题。A可见；C错；D用途须核。

questions.prompt: What role did the photograph have?
options: It replaced the physical sample exactly under all viewing conditions.
It removed the need for process notes.
It aided documentation while retaining limits from lighting and display.
It proved screen lighting never affected colour.
questions.explanation: C正确：照有记录益但受光屏，物件及条件笔记仍保。A普替不行；B需史；D反。

questions.prompt: Why keep the first tile after planning a more relevant trial?
options: It remained evidence about its own conditions and could inform the next question.
It guaranteed every future vessel would be identical.
Its earlier conditions had become unknowable.
A later trial made all earlier evidence false.
questions.explanation: A正确：首片不是废错，限其条件证据并启下问。B不保；C有记；D新试不抹旧真。

questions.prompt: Which principle does the passage support?
options: One appealing sample settles every material and use question.
No visual observation can contribute evidence.
A named glaze removes all effects of process.
A sample supports claims within its conditions, with changed features needing relevant checks.
questions.explanation: D正确：样有界，预测连材料形施工况并核变项。A、C过保；B非弃观察。

units.title: 六级阅读：排序反馈中的可见性与亲属称谓的社会关系

materials.title: The Popular Item That Had Been Placed First
materials.text:
A fictional digital-library study examined which articles readers selected from a ranked list. The article at the top received many clicks. A summary described that count as an independent measure of the article’s underlying popularity and proposed using it to justify keeping the same article first indefinitely.

The research team asked how the count had been generated. Position affected the opportunity to be seen. An article placed low on the list could receive few clicks partly because few readers reached it, rather than because everyone who saw it disliked it. The observed choice combined the article, the audience and the presentation that had made the choice available. A count produced under one ranking was therefore not a neutral view of preferences untouched by that ranking.

Using those clicks to update future positions could create feedback. An initial advantage in visibility might produce more recorded interaction, which then justified further visibility. This mechanism did not prove that the leading article had no appeal. It showed why repeated success under the same exposure arrangement could not, by itself, establish how the articles would compare under equal opportunity to be encountered.

The team considered a limited experiment that varied presentation within the study’s authorised setting. Its design had to identify which outcome and population it addressed. A comparison of click rates after a position change could inform a question about exposure. It did not automatically establish long-term satisfaction or the quality of the information readers took away. A quick click and a useful reading experience were related events with different evidence requirements.

The analysis also distinguished missing observation from a negative preference. A reader who never encountered an article had not supplied the same signal as one who saw it and deliberately declined. Even the latter action could have several explanations, including time constraints or an already familiar topic. The system needed a reasoned account of what its behavioural measures represented rather than treating every absent click as the same kind of rejection.

The revised report retained both interaction records and information about their opportunities. It described position, exposure and the selection measure together. The ranking could still use behavioural evidence, but its interpretation would acknowledge the process that had produced it.

The case illustrated an important feature of interactive systems: a system can help create the data later used to evaluate or train it. Analysing that data requires attention to the choices made available and the unequal chances to make them. A successful count may be partly evidence of appeal and partly evidence of the platform’s own past decisions.

questions.prompt: Why was the top article’s click count not an independent popularity measure?
options: Every reader had seen all articles equally.
Its ranking position influenced the opportunity for readers to encounter and select it.
The study proved the article had no appeal.
Clicks were impossible to record.
questions.explanation: B正确：排名影响暴露，点击混文章受众呈现，不独立于排法。A不等曝；C可有吸引；D有记录。

questions.prompt: What feedback mechanism is described?
options: Low placement guaranteed more attention.
Every position change eliminated preferences.
The system never used earlier data.
Visibility could generate interaction that then justified further visibility.
questions.explanation: D正确：初可见优势→互动多→再排优，非证零内在偏好。A反；C用既有；B不消偏好。

questions.prompt: What limit applies to a position experiment’s click result?
options: It necessarily measures all long-term satisfaction.
It proves information quality from one click.
It addresses a defined exposure-related outcome, which differs from every later reading benefit.
It makes the studied population irrelevant.
questions.explanation: C正确：实验需定群和量，位置点击不直接定长期满足或所得质量。A、B过推；D群要明。

questions.prompt: Why distinguish unseen items from seen-but-declined items?
options: Different opportunities and actions can generate the same absent-click record.
Every declined item proves dislike.
Time constraints never affect clicks.
They necessarily express identical deliberate rejection.
questions.explanation: A正确：未见不同见后不点，后者亦时限熟题等，不能一律拒绝。D混同；B过因；C可影响。

questions.prompt: Which broader principle does the case illustrate?
options: Every leading item must have been selected unfairly.
Behavioural data are always worthless.
An interactive system may shape the observations later used to assess or update it.
A click count removes the need to examine presentation.
questions.explanation: C正确：系统过去决策造后数据部分，需追可供选与机会。B非弃数据；A未判全不公；D呈现关键。

materials.title: A Family Term Was Not a Blood Test
materials.text:
A fictional anthropology seminar compared kinship descriptions in a set of invented households. A translation used the familiar English word mother for several differently situated people. One student assumed that every occurrence identified the same biological relationship and proposed converting the terms directly into a genetic family tree.

The tutor asked how each term was used in the described community and interaction. Kinship language could organise obligations, care, residence or recognised descent as well as refer to biological connections. A term’s social role could not be determined solely by selecting its nearest everyday English equivalent. The same translation might compress distinctions that mattered locally, while different translated words might conceal a relationship the community treated as connected.

The exercise distinguished a person’s account from the analyst’s diagram. A diagram was a representation constructed for a purpose. It could make some relationships easy to compare while leaving out everyday practices through which people understood membership. The tutor did not discard diagrams as useless. It required their conventions and omissions to be stated, rather than allowing lines and symbols to appear as an unedited view of family life.

Household membership and kinship were also separated. People sharing a dwelling at one time did not necessarily exhaust the set of those recognised as relatives. Conversely, living apart did not automatically end a relation. The seminar recorded time and the relevant account of membership, so one household survey was not presented as a permanent map of every enduring obligation.

Adoption and care arrangements made the limitation of a purely biological reading especially visible in the invented cases. A recognised parent could hold duties and status that were not reducible to genetic contribution. Describing those relationships as merely unreal because they differed from one narrow criterion would replace the community’s social account with the analyst’s unexplained preference for that criterion.

The class nevertheless avoided the opposite universal claim that biological ideas never mattered. Their significance was a question for the particular setting and evidence. Different people might also contest a relationship, and the report attributed their accounts rather than pretending a single label settled every disagreement.

The final comparison kept terms, practices, diagrams and attributed interpretations connected. Its aim was not to discover one universal translation table for every family system. It was to examine what a relation meant in a stated context and what was lost when a familiar word was allowed to stand for the entire explanation.

questions.prompt: Why was direct conversion of mother into a genetic relation inadequate?
options: Its social role could involve locally defined care, obligations or descent not fixed by the English equivalent alone.
Every use of the term was meaningless.
The seminar proved biological ideas never mattered.
Every household used identical terminology.
questions.explanation: A正确：称谓本地社会职能可涉照护义务承认关系，不靠英词定遗传。B非无义；C拒另极端；D有差。

questions.prompt: How should an analyst’s diagram be treated?
options: As an unedited photograph of all family practices.
As necessarily useless.
As a purposeful representation with conventions and omissions that need explanation.
As proof every disputed relation has one uncontested meaning.
questions.explanation: C正确：图选择便比但漏实践，明约定界限而非透明全景。A错误；B可有用；D关系可争。

questions.prompt: What distinction concerns a household survey?
options: Everyone related must live in the same dwelling.
Living apart automatically ends kinship.
A survey permanently captures every obligation.
Co-residence at a time and the wider set of recognised relations are not identical.
questions.explanation: D正确：同住非亲属全集，分住不自动绝，需时点成员定义。A、B、C一一否。

questions.prompt: What do the adoption examples illustrate?
options: All care relations are unreal.
Recognised parental status and duties need not reduce to genetic contribution.
Only the analyst can define legitimate membership without evidence.
Every community denies biological relations.
questions.explanation: B正确：承认父母义务地位可非遗传，不可因窄准则说不真。A反；C偏好须说明；D非全否生物。

questions.prompt: What is the final aim of the comparison?
options: To understand relations through their stated terms, practices and attributed interpretations.
To supply one universal word-for-word family translation table.
To make familiar English words a substitute for context.
To remove all disagreement from the record.
questions.explanation: A正确：连接称谓实践图及归属解释，问境义而非普词表。B拒；C熟词不能全释；D争论可留。

units.title: 六级阅读：夜间灯光代理指标与小说叙述者的可靠性

materials.title: A Brighter Pixel Was Not a New Factory Count
materials.text:
A fictional regional study used satellite observations of light at night to investigate economic activity. A presentation showed one district becoming brighter over several years. A viewer concluded that the image directly counted all goods produced there and that every additional unit of brightness meant the same economic gain in every location.

The researchers described the observation as a proxy. Artificial lighting could relate to activity, settlement and infrastructure, but the relationship depended on how light was produced, used and recorded. A change in lighting technology or street-light policy could alter the signal without an identical change in production. Some economically important activities used little visible outdoor light, while a brightly illuminated place did not necessarily contain a proportional amount of every kind of output.

The instrument introduced further limits. Its sensitivity, spatial resolution and processing affected what the image represented. A bright source could influence nearby pixels, and changes across sensor systems required care before being interpreted as a continuous social trend. The team retained those details rather than treating an attractive annual map as a direct photograph of the economy itself.

Comparisons also depended on scale. A relationship estimated across broad regions could be less reliable for a small area with a particular mix of land uses. Applying the broad association unchanged to every pixel would add a claim the original comparison had not tested. The researchers examined relevant reference data and the uncertainty of the transfer instead of assuming that a general correlation supplied a universal conversion formula.

The study did not dismiss the satellite record because it was indirect. In places with limited conventional information, repeated observations could contribute valuable evidence. The benefit was strongest when the question matched the signal’s scope and other sources could help interpret unusual changes. An indirect measure could be useful without being an exhaustive or infallible account.

The final report distinguished observed radiance, modelled economic estimates and explanations for change. Each stage required its own assumptions. A rise in an estimated quantity was not presented as though a satellite had independently identified every causal event behind it.

The case showed how a powerful new data source could widen inquiry while requiring more precise language. A brighter image could support an investigation of economic change. It could not make the choice of proxy, the instrument’s properties and the modelling relationship disappear from the chain of reasoning that connected light in the night sky with activity on the ground.

questions.prompt: Why did brightness not directly count economic output?
options: The researchers declared indirect data useless.
The satellite had no instrument.
Every activity emitted identical outdoor light.
Lighting practices and technology could change the signal independently of proportional production changes.
questions.explanation: D正确：光是代理，技术政策活动类型皆可改关系，不逐件产出计。B有测；C不等；A仍有用。

questions.prompt: What role did sensor properties play?
options: They guaranteed identical values across all systems.
They shaped sensitivity, spatial representation and comparability across time.
They made processing irrelevant.
They converted all pixels into factories.
questions.explanation: B正确：灵敏分辨处理及溢邻像素、跨传感比影响图义。A未保；C处理要记；D非工厂直接数。

questions.prompt: Why question transfer from broad regions to a small pixel?
options: A broad association did not automatically validate an unchanged conversion at every local scale.
Reference data could never help.
Every scale necessarily had the same relationship.
The original study measured every local cause directly.
questions.explanation: A正确：大区相关不保小域用地组合与逐像素换算，需参照及疑度。C错；B可助；D未直因。

questions.prompt: How did the team regard indirect data?
options: As worthless because no proxy can help.
As sufficient for every causal explanation.
As potentially valuable when its scope, assumptions and interpretation were clear.
As a substitute for every other source.
questions.explanation: C正确：信息稀缺处重复光数据有益，但要配问题他源解异常。A反；B、D过足。

questions.prompt: Which stages did the final report distinguish?
options: Factories, votes and individual salaries directly counted from each pixel.
Observed radiance, modelled economic estimates and causal explanations of change.
Unprocessed sunlight and every daytime activity.
Only one raw number with no assumptions.
questions.explanation: B正确：三阶段各需假设，卫星未直接识全部因事。A、C文无直计；D保链与假设。

materials.title: The Narrator Who Believed Her Own Account
materials.text:
A fictional literature seminar discussed a novel told by a character who described her past decisions with complete confidence. Later scenes gave readers reasons to doubt parts of that account. A student labelled the narrator a liar and assumed that the historical author must share every judgement the narrator expressed.

The tutor separated the narrator’s role from the author’s and asked what kind of unreliability the text supported. A narrator could deliberately mislead, misunderstand events, forget relevant information or interpret them through a narrow perspective. Confidence in the telling did not distinguish among all those possibilities. A false statement within the account was not automatically proof of conscious deception by the character.

The class examined textual cues. Other characters’ responses, gaps between described actions and stated motives, and later consequences could challenge the narrator’s explanation. No single cue was treated as a mechanical diagnostic valid for every novel. The interpretation depended on how the work organised those signals and what alternative readings remained plausible.

The tutor also distinguished the narrator’s knowledge at the time of an event from the knowledge available at the later moment of telling. A retrospective voice could interpret an earlier action differently after learning more. The novel might make that distance visible or allow a reader to discover it gradually. Treating all sentences as if they came from one timeless viewpoint would miss that structure.

Readers did not have to accept the narrator’s moral vocabulary merely because it appeared in first person. The work could create distance between the account and what the reader was invited to infer. That distance was an argued interpretation of the text, not direct access to the author’s private beliefs. A claim about the historical person behind the novel required a different kind of evidence from a claim about the effect of its narrative arrangement.

The seminar retained uncertainty where the text left motives unresolved. It did not reduce careful reading to finding a hidden official answer about whether the speaker was good or bad. The useful task was to explain how confidence, limited knowledge and narrative cues shaped the reader’s judgement.

The final essay therefore described a narrator whose account was questionable in specified ways, with examples supporting each claim. It avoided equating error with lying and voice with author. That precision allowed the novel’s structure to matter: a story could invite readers to understand more than its confident speaker explicitly recognised.

questions.prompt: Why was liar not automatically the correct diagnosis?
options: Every narrator was incapable of error.
The novel contained no reasons for doubt.
An unreliable account could result from misunderstanding or limited knowledge as well as deliberate deception.
Confidence established complete accuracy.
questions.explanation: C正确：不可靠可误解遗忘狭见或故骗，假不自动知假。A错；B后场提供疑；D信心非真。

questions.prompt: What supported interpretation of unreliability?
options: Relations among textual responses, motives, actions and later consequences.
The author’s private beliefs directly observed in each first-person sentence.
One universal cue that diagnoses every novel mechanically.
A rule that all first-person stories must be false.
questions.explanation: A正确：应按文组织他人反应行为动机缝后果等线索辩解释。C拒万能；B无直访；D未一律假。

questions.prompt: Why distinguish event time from telling time?
options: A narrator could never learn anything later.
Later knowledge could change how an earlier action was understood in the narration.
Retrospection removed all possible interpretation.
Every sentence came from a timeless perspective.
questions.explanation: B正确：回望可在后来学得后释旧事，叙述时距结构要看。A相反；D忽略时距；C仍解释。

questions.prompt: What limits a claim about the historical author’s beliefs?
options: First-person grammar proves personal authorship of every described event.
Every narrator sentence necessarily states the author’s opinion.
A textual interpretation can replace all biographical evidence.
The narrator’s voice and the work’s effects are not direct access to the author’s private views.
questions.explanation: D正确：人物声与文效果非私人信念直证，历史作者需别种证。B、C、A混层。

questions.prompt: What made the final essay precise?
options: It labelled the speaker good or bad without examples.
It guaranteed a hidden official answer about every motive.
It specified questionable features and their textual support while separating error, deception, voice and author.
It ignored the structure of the telling.
questions.explanation: C正确：定何处可疑及例证，分错骗和声作者，使结构有义。A没论证；B可未决；D重结构。

units.title: 六级阅读：道路扩容后的出行变化与测试集污染

materials.title: The Road Widened, and the Trips Changed
materials.text:
A fictional transport study examined travel after a busy road gained additional capacity. Immediately after opening, some trips became faster. Later measurements showed traffic patterns changing again. A commentary announced that the early improvement proved congestion had been permanently solved, while another treated the later traffic as proof the new road could never have helped anyone.

The researchers described a changing system rather than accepting either shortcut. Travel decisions could respond to conditions. Some people might change departure times, select another route, switch transport mode or make a journey previously avoided. Over a longer period, locations of activities could change as well. The amount of traffic was therefore not necessarily a fixed quantity poured into an enlarged container.

These responses could consume some of the initially available space. That mechanism did not imply that every road project had the same effect or that the effect could be inferred from a universal percentage without local evidence. The study specified its location, period and comparison. It also separated changes on the widened road from changes elsewhere in the network. A vehicle moving from another route was not automatically a completely new journey.

The baseline mattered. A before-and-after comparison could include economic changes, other transport interventions and shifts in population. Observing more traffic after opening did not, by timing alone, identify how much was caused by the added capacity. The team considered the relevant alternatives and what would plausibly have happened without the project. That comparison was an analytical task, not a second history directly visible beside the first.

The researchers also asked which outcome mattered. Journey time, reliability, access to opportunities and environmental consequences were different measures. An improvement for some users could coexist with a cost for others or a change in total travel. Calling the project successful or unsuccessful without naming the objective would hide a value choice inside what sounded like a purely numerical verdict.

The final report retained both the early observations and the later responses. It did not erase a genuine initial gain because conditions changed, nor present that gain as a permanent promise. The road had altered choices within a network, and those choices contributed to the outcome being measured.

The broader lesson was to evaluate infrastructure in a system that reacts. A capacity change could affect demand and distribution as well as the immediate speed of a fixed set of trips. A careful conclusion followed those responses, stated the counterfactual comparison and named whose experience and which timescale its claims addressed.

questions.prompt: Why was the fixed-container image inadequate?
options: Travel choices and potentially the number or arrangement of trips could respond to changed conditions.
Every traveller had an unchanging route and departure time.
The study proved no one ever benefited.
All later traffic consisted of entirely new journeys.
questions.explanation: A正确：路线时段方式做不做等可变，交通量非固定灌容器。B反；C早益可真；D移路非全新增。

questions.prompt: Why distinguish network redistribution from new journeys?
options: The two were identical by definition.
A network contained only one road.
More vehicles on one road could include trips shifted from elsewhere.
The distinction eliminated the need for location information.
questions.explanation: C正确：本路增量可别路移来，不等出行总量全新。A混；B网络多处；D须范围。

questions.prompt: What limited a simple before-and-after causal claim?
options: The added road could not possibly affect travel.
All background conditions had been proven constant.
Timing alone measured the complete counterfactual.
Other economic, demographic and transport changes could contribute to the observed difference.
questions.explanation: D正确：同期他因可混，需无项目可信比较非时序自因。A未否；B未证恒；C反事实非可直观。

questions.prompt: Why name the outcome and affected users?
options: Success had one universal numerical definition.
Different objectives and groups could experience different gains and costs.
Only the first driver’s experience mattered.
Journey time and environmental consequences were always identical.
questions.explanation: B正确：时可靠可达环境问异，可有人益他有代价，评需明价值目标。A、D、C单一化错。

questions.prompt: How should early improvement and later change be combined?
options: Preserve both as evidence within their timescales and examine the responsive system.
Erase the early improvement as necessarily false.
Treat the early improvement as a guarantee for all future conditions.
Assume later traffic proves every possible objective failed.
questions.explanation: A正确：真早益不因后变抹，也不保永久，跟踪系统响应。B、C两误；D未全目标失败。

materials.title: The Test Questions Had Been Seen before
materials.text:
A fictional model-evaluation team used a benchmark intended to assess performance on tasks not previously encountered in the relevant form. One system achieved an unusually high score. Later investigation found that some benchmark material had entered the development data. A manager argued that the score remained a pure measure of generalisation because the final program had still produced the right answers.

The evaluator separated correctness on the test from the interpretation attached to that correctness. A model might answer a familiar item through processes different from those needed for a genuinely new case. Prior exposure did not make every answer factually wrong. It affected whether the score supported the claim that performance extended to previously unseen material under the intended conditions.

The team examined the route of exposure. Exact copies were one possibility, but near-duplicate tasks or answer-bearing discussions could also matter depending on the benchmark’s purpose. At the same time, the mere use of a common topic or ordinary vocabulary did not establish problematic contamination. The relevant question was what information had been available and whether it undermined the independence required by the evaluation claim.

Repeated development against the benchmark raised a related issue. Even without putting its exact items into training, choices could be tuned to results from the supposed final test. The benchmark would then have participated in development rather than remaining an untouched assessment. Calling it test data did not preserve its role if the information flow contradicted that label.

The investigation retained versions and provenance for the benchmark and the development process. A later clean replacement could provide useful new evidence, but its score was not a retroactive measurement of the earlier system under conditions that had never actually held. The report distinguished the old result, its weakened interpretation and the new assessment.

The team also avoided declaring the entire system useless because some evidence was compromised. Other tasks and properly separated tests could still reveal real capabilities. The response was to narrow or replace unsupported claims, not to assume that every strong result had only one cause.

The case showed that an evaluation number depends on a relationship between test, system and development history. Reproducing the arithmetic of a score was not enough to reproduce its meaning. The relevant separation had to be demonstrated, not merely named. For a claim about new tasks, the evaluator needed evidence that the relevant information had remained outside the process used to shape the tested system.

questions.prompt: How could prior exposure affect an otherwise correct benchmark answer?
options: It automatically made the answer false.
It weakened the inference from correctness to performance on genuinely unseen material.
It proved every capability was absent.
It made development history irrelevant.
questions.explanation: B正确：熟题正确可真但不等新题泛化，解释受损非事实答案变假。A、C过否；D史关键。

questions.prompt: What kind of exposure required investigation?
options: Only identical character-for-character copies could ever matter.
Any common vocabulary proved contamination.
No topic overlap could ever be harmless.
Information such as relevant duplicates or answer-bearing discussion, judged against the evaluation purpose.
questions.explanation: D正确：需看可得信息与所需独立，近题答讨论可能，普通词题材不自污染。A窄；B、C过宽。

questions.prompt: Why could repeated tuning against test results change the test’s role?
options: A label guarantees independence forever.
Only file location determines whether data shaped development.
Information from the supposed final assessment could become part of the development process.
Feedback never influences model choices.
questions.explanation: C正确：虽未训原题但按结果调选择即参与开发，test名不能保。A、B错；D反馈可影响。

questions.prompt: What could a later clean test establish?
options: New evidence under its actual conditions, rather than rewriting the conditions of an earlier score.
A retroactive untouched test of the earlier contaminated result.
That every old answer was factually wrong.
That provenance records were unnecessary.
questions.explanation: A正确：新干净评是新条件证，不能倒造旧时未有独立条件。B反；C不一定假；D保版本来源。

questions.prompt: What is the appropriate response to compromised evidence?
options: Assume every strong result has only memorisation as a cause.
Revise the unsupported interpretation while seeking properly separated evidence of capabilities.
Declare every system capability nonexistent.
Keep the original generalisation claim solely because arithmetic was correct.
questions.explanation: B正确：缩换未支撑claims，别测仍可真能力，算分重现非义重现。A、C全否；D忽历史。

units.title: 六级阅读：受体结合与效应及历史剧场的声学重建

materials.title: A Molecule Bound but Did Not Switch It On
materials.text:
A fictional pharmacology seminar compared molecules interacting with a receptor in a simplified system. One molecule bound strongly but did not activate the measured response in the way another did. A student concluded that the experiment was contradictory: if a molecule fitted the receptor well, it must produce the largest possible biological effect.

The tutor separated affinity from the capacity to produce a response under the model. Binding described a relationship with the receptor, while activation and downstream effect involved further properties and conditions. Strong binding did not automatically imply strong activation. A molecule could occupy a receptor and interfere with another molecule’s effect without acting as the same kind of activator itself.

The measured response also depended on the biological system. Receptor availability, the link to later signalling and the conditions of the assay could affect the observed result. A value obtained in one preparation did not by itself describe every tissue or a complete outcome in a person. The seminar retained the level of the claim rather than carrying one laboratory curve directly into a universal prediction.

The class distinguished potency from maximum effect. The amount needed to obtain a specified response was not the same quantity as the largest response achievable in the stated system. A molecule could reach a given effect at a lower concentration while not having the largest attainable maximum. Comparing curves required attention to which feature was being discussed and whether the underlying conditions were comparable.

Concentration at the receptor introduced another step beyond an administered amount. The route from a supplied dose to a local concentration could involve distribution and removal. The tutor did not claim that equal administered quantities guaranteed identical receptor exposure. That connection required its own account, especially when moving from the simplified experiment to a broader setting.

The final report consequently used different words for binding, activation, measured response and practical outcome. A familiar single label such as stronger would have concealed which comparison had actually been made. The molecule that bound well but did not switch on the selected response was not an impossible exception to the lesson. It was a reason the lesson needed several distinct concepts.

The seminar offered no treatment recommendation or claim about a real medicine. It illustrated a general analytical habit: follow the stages between an interaction and an outcome, and attach each quantity to the process it measures. A precise distinction can explain an apparent contradiction that disappears once different meanings of strength are no longer treated as one.

questions.prompt: Why was strong binding without the expected activation not contradictory?
options: The tutor said receptors did not exist in the model.
All binding necessarily produced the largest response.
Affinity and ability to generate the measured response were distinct properties.
Every molecule had identical action by definition.
questions.explanation: C正确：亲和结合与激活效应分，能占位阻他效而非同激动。B学生误解；A有模型受体；D不同。

questions.prompt: Why retain the assay’s biological system?
options: Receptor availability and signalling conditions can affect the measured response.
It guarantees identical behaviour in every tissue.
A laboratory curve directly measures every personal outcome.
Only a molecule’s name can affect results.
questions.explanation: A正确：受体量和后信号体系影响反应，一制备不普人体。B、C过推；D条件亦要紧。

questions.prompt: What distinction concerns potency and maximum effect?
options: They are two names for the same numerical feature.
The concentration needed for a stated response differs from the largest achievable response.
A lower required concentration always guarantees a larger maximum.
Neither quantity depends on a defined system.
questions.explanation: B正确：达到定反应所需量与最大达反应不同，低量不保高max。A混同；C错误；D体系须明。

questions.prompt: Why is administered dose not automatically receptor exposure?
options: Distribution and removal never occur.
Equal doses always yield equal local concentrations.
A dose is measured only after every receptor binds.
The route to local concentration involves additional processes and conditions.
questions.explanation: D正确：给入量到局部还经分布清除，等剂不保等暴露。A、B反；C剂量非绑定后才量。

questions.prompt: What analytical approach does the passage illustrate?
options: Infer treatment advice directly from one simplified curve.
Use stronger as an exact replacement for all quantities.
Trace distinct stages and measures between an interaction and an outcome.
Discard every result that challenges an everyday expectation.
questions.explanation: C正确：逐结合激活测效实际结果链定量义，释表面矛盾。B模糊词不行；A没疗建议；D不弃现象。

materials.title: Hearing a Theatre That No Longer Exists
materials.text:
A fictional heritage project reconstructed the possible acoustics of a demolished theatre. It combined surviving plans, material descriptions and a computational sound model. A demonstration allowed listeners to hear a simulated voice from a proposed stage position. Publicity described the result as exactly what an audience had heard at the building’s opening performance.

The researchers revised that description. The model offered a scenario supported by selected evidence, not an audio recording recovered from the past. Some dimensions were well documented, while seating materials and later changes were less certain. Several plausible reconstructions could remain consistent with parts of the record. The team retained those alternatives rather than allowing one polished demonstration to hide the uncertainty of its inputs.

The represented audience mattered. People and furnishings affected sound absorption and the pattern of reflections. An empty-room simulation did not automatically reproduce a crowded performance. The position and direction of the sound source also influenced what reached a listener. A result from one seat could not stand without qualification for every possible place in the room.

The project distinguished room response from the source signal used to make it audible. A modern actor’s recorded voice contributed articulation, timing and vocal qualities not preserved in the architectural plans. Combining that signal with a modelled room could help exploration, but it did not recover the voice of a historical performer. The final listening experience was assembled from components with different origins.

The team compared selected model outputs with relevant acoustic principles and available evidence. Such checks could identify implausible assumptions or assess how changes affected the result. They could not create a direct measurement of the vanished original. Agreement with a general expectation was useful support, not a substitute for evidence about every undocumented surface.

The public display offered several stated scenarios and explained which features changed between them. Visitors could hear how an assumed material or occupancy altered the result. The demonstration became an inquiry tool rather than a single authoritative soundtrack. Its most important contribution was not a promise of perfect historical presence, but a way to make the consequences of interpretive choices perceptible.

The researchers did not abandon the reconstruction because it was conditional. They made the conditions part of the experience. A credible account connected surviving evidence, modelling choices and the modern source recording, allowing listeners to understand both the possibilities explored and the aspects of the past that the available record could not uniquely restore.

questions.prompt: Why was the opening publicity too strong?
options: The model contained no documented information.
The researchers had an original recording of every seat.
The theatre still existed unchanged.
A conditional reconstruction was presented as an exact recovered historical listening experience.
questions.explanation: D正确：情景模拟非开幕录音，输入部分未定不独复原。A有图料；C已拆；B无原录。

questions.prompt: Why did occupancy matter?
options: People could never affect acoustics.
People and furnishings could alter absorption and reflections.
An empty room was always identical to a full performance.
Source direction was irrelevant whenever seats were known.
questions.explanation: B正确：人和家具吸反改变，空室不自动等满场；位向也影响。A、C反；D需源方向。

questions.prompt: What did the modern actor’s recording contribute?
options: Modern vocal properties that were separate from the modelled room response.
Only architectural dimensions.
Proof that every past articulation was known.
The historical performer’s uniquely recovered voice.
questions.explanation: A正确：现代声源含咬字节奏声质，非图纸复古人声，room与source分。D、C过复原；B非尺寸。

questions.prompt: What could model checks establish?
options: A guarantee that one general expectation proved the whole scenario.
Exact knowledge of every undocumented surface.
Support or problems under the tested assumptions without creating direct measurements of the vanished room.
That conditional models must be discarded.
questions.explanation: C正确：核原则证据可排不合理或审敏感，不能造已逝实测。B、A过保；D仍有用。

questions.prompt: What made the revised public display useful?
options: It let listeners compare stated scenarios and hear consequences of assumptions.
It concealed every modelling choice for immersion.
It called one soundtrack the only historical truth.
It treated all evidence and all source recordings as having the same origin.
questions.explanation: A正确：多情景明变项可听假设后果，成为探究工具。B藏限；C拒单权威；D来源异。
